A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same REED study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices A-G are available and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation, protein inverse-folding, and molecule-generation experiments, including quantitative comparisons, appendix ablations, and generated samples.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds component, curriculum, and representation-quality ablations, together with computational-cost results.

M1.justification: REED's multimodal alignment objective, joint training curriculum, domain-specific architectures, and inference procedures are retained. The additional encoder and schedule variants are ablation configurations, rather than revisions to the proposed default method.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet 256 × 256 image generation, PDB protein inverse folding, and GEOM-DRUG molecule generation. The new experiments vary training guidance and schedules within existing coverage; they add no dataset, task, population, or evaluation environment.

E2.justification: v2 Table 12 adds evaluated representation-source alternatives using Qwen2-VL 2B, OpenCLIP, and SigLIP against the default Qwen2-VL 7B configuration. The primary image, protein, and molecule generation baseline sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix E.1 changes the reported captioning limit from 128 tokens to 200 new tokens; this establishes a documentation-level setting revision, not that experiments were rerun. New ablations introduce constant or 25K/50K/75K phase-in schedules, alignment-weight decay, and Gaussian feature noise of scale 0.1. Core splits, metrics, sampling procedures, and evaluation sample counts are retained.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's alignment-depth, objective-approximation, and protein ablations, v2 substantially expands scrutiny of REED's central design choices. Tables 3 and 11 test component removal and curriculum sensitivity; Table 12 tests alternative encoders and noisy guidance, examining dependence on representation quality.

E5.justification: Both versions report protein results as means over three random seeds with standard deviations. The added image ablations retain point-estimate reporting without introducing seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Headline benchmark scores are retained, but substantial supporting results are added, including FIDs of 29.4 without the curriculum, 26.3 with Qwen2-VL 2B, and 25.0 with noisy 7B features, plus runtime measurements. Existing ablation entries also change: the VLM-layer-15 FID becomes 29.4 instead of 24.6, and image-only layer-4 FID becomes 27.7 instead of 24.8. These are reported revisions, not established same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: Section 2 and Appendices B-C retain the mathematical definitions, assumptions, variational decomposition, Propositions 1-3, Theorem 1, and their proofs. The added Platonic representation hypothesis discussion is conceptual motivation rather than a new formal result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same theoretical and methodological contributions and cross-domain improvement claims, including the 23.3-fold speedup over SiT and fourfold speedup over REPA. New experiments support existing claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of robustness to imperfect representations and attributes limited OpenCLIP/SigLIP benefits to their training objectives and semantic content. It also explains model-size and computational tradeoffs and elaborates possible adaptive curricula. These extend the discussion without replacing the existing mechanism explanation.

D1.justification: v2 specifies the captioning prompt and conversation template, clarifies online DINOv2 extraction, identifies the OpenCLIP source, and adds a project-page link. Appendix E.1 newly reports captioning and embedding-extraction times of 7.5 and 1.3 hours and diffusion-training runtimes. VLM caching and the main hardware specifications were already disclosed in v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to The Platonic Representation Hypothesis and Sigmoid Loss for Language Image Pre-Training, connecting the former to multimodal guidance and evaluating SigLIP representations. The existing positioning relative to REPA, RCG, and domain-specific generators remains intact.

P1.justification: Changes are localized explanatory additions in Sections 3.1 and 4.1 and Appendices E.1 and F.1, separation of captioning and embedding descriptions, and an acknowledgement and conference header. The overall narrative, section hierarchy, and most existing prose are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds three ablation tables and Figure 3 illustrating image-caption pairs. Existing tables and qualitative figures are renumbered or repositioned, including moving the first generated-image grid onto its own page. The established visual design and original sample displays are retained.

improvement.justification: The new ablations better support REED's curriculum and representation choices, while runtime accounting includes previously unquantified captioning and embedding costs. These provide useful gains over v1. However, ablation reporting remains inconsistent: v2 Tables 4 and 9 give FIDs of 25.9 and 26.5 for the same alignment depths, and Table 8 reports 29.4 for the default VLM layer versus 24.6 elsewhere without explaining different settings. These issues limit the overall improvement.
